title: Minimal INI serialization and parsing
instructions:
Implement `loads(text: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]` in `ini_reader.py` and
`dumps(data: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> str` in `ini_writer.py`. The writer may import
validation helpers from the reader. This is a deliberately small INI format, with no interpolation.
Reader rules:
- Lines are separated by LF (CRLF is also accepted). Strip surrounding whitespace on each line.
  Ignore blank lines and lines whose first nonwhitespace character is `#` or `;`.
- A line beginning `[` must be exactly a section header `[name]`. Trim the name; it must be
  nonempty and contain neither `[` nor `]`. A repeated section resumes its existing dictionary.
- Every other content line must contain `=` and occur after a section header. Split at the first
  `=`, stripping whitespace from key and value. Keys must be nonempty and cannot start with
  `[`, `#`, or `;`. Duplicate keys overwrite the previous value. Empty values are allowed.
  Inline `#`, `;`, `=`, and quotes in values are literal. No quoting or escape syntax is recognized.
- Section names, keys, and values may not contain CR or LF. Invalid syntax raises `ValueError`.
  Empty/comment-only input returns `{}`. Preserve insertion order of sections and keys; replacing
  a key or reopening a section does not move it.
Writer rules:
- Input consists of dictionaries and strings as in the signature. Preserve their insertion order.
- Section names must be nonempty, already stripped, and contain no brackets or CR/LF.
  Keys must be nonempty, already stripped, contain no `=` or CR/LF, and not start with `[`, `#`, `;`.
  Values must already be stripped and contain no CR/LF; they may be empty.
  Any unrepresentable name, key, or value raises `ValueError`.
- Emit `[name]`, then each `key=value`, one per line. Separate sections with exactly one blank
  line, and end nonempty output with exactly one newline. Emit empty sections too. `{}` emits `""`.
Every valid writer input must round-trip through the reader exactly, including empty sections.

## Files
- `ini_reader.py`
- `ini_writer.py`
